key_insight: A forked PINN with a dedicated control branch resolves gradient conflicts in non-Markovian open quantum dynamics, enabling joint simulation and control in one differentiable framework.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical end-to-end tool for quantum state preparation and pulse design in open systems where standard PINNs and conventional control methods struggle.
method: Split the PINN into simulation and control branches.
Use selective gradient flow to decouple optimization objectives at the gradient level.
Train jointly on the coupled open-quantum-system equations for both dynamics and control.
evidence_signal: On a two-qubit Heisenberg XXX model, the method reproduces non-Markovian features and achieves higher control fidelity than gradient ascent pulse engineering, chopped random basis, and standard PINNs.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated on a specific two-qubit model, so scalability and robustness on larger noisy hardware remain to be validated.
paper_title: Forked Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Non-Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics and Control
